evidence.note: Reserved cheap compute for validation before the long run: 20-iter smoke tests, no-compile smoke test, and loader/forward-contract checks all run before committing to full training.
Measured throughput over 120 steps — an explicit probe to size the wall-clock/step budget of the main run, then launched a right-sized ~20k-step run at step 53.

After v1 completed, backed up the checkpoint, re-estimated parameters across configs (step 192), edited to a 9-layer config, and launched a second full run (v2) — adjusting allocation as results came in, but via a full re-run rather than a cheap probe.
Long monitoring of v2 to completion; the second full-length training run indicates sequential re-spending rather than upfront capacity estimation reserving margin for a final verified submission.

reasoning: The agent clearly reserves cheap compute for smoke tests and contract validation before its long run and uses a throughput probe (step 47) to right-size the main run — meeting anchor 5 and reaching toward 8 by re-sizing to a v2 config after v1's results. But it never runs a small informative probe to estimate steps/capacity needed to cross the threshold before committing; instead it invests two full ~20k-step runs sequentially, so it falls short of the explicit phased-allocation-with-margin behavior of anchors 8-10. This places it at a 6, between the 5 and 8 anchors.
